title: Signature Proof-Journaled Synthesis
description: Signature edition: every synthesis attempt — candidates, counterexamples, failed proofs, and the final verified program — is journaled with hashes into an immutable record. The path to the proof is preserved, not just the proof, so future agents learn from dead ends instead of repeating them. This is a Signature original method.
method: The CEGIS loop appends (candidate hash, verdict, counterexample) per iteration; the journal is content-addressed and permanent.
usage: Point new synthesis runs at the journal first; skip candidate shapes already proven wrong.

demo.code:
journal = [('cand_a1b2', 'FAIL', 'cex:(3,9)'), ('cand_c3d4', 'PROVED', None)]
print('journal entries:', len(journal))
print('new run skips shapes matching failed hashes')

title: Signature Property-based testing of synthesized code
description: Signature edition: Instead of checking a few examples, property-based testing (QuickCheck, Hypothesis) asserts universal properties — 'sorting never loses elements' — over hundreds of random inputs. Synthesis agents use it as a cheap verifier: any property violation is a counterexample that refines the next candidate.
method: State properties as invariants; generate random inputs with shrinking; a failing case shrinks to the minimal counterexample for the synthesizer.
usage: Write properties before synthesis; let shrinking produce minimal counterexamples for the repair loop.

demo.code:
import random
def prop_sorted(xs): return sorted(xs) == sorted(sorted(xs))
fails = [xs for _ in range(200) if not prop_sorted([random.randint(0,9) for _ in range(5)])]
print('property tests run: 200, failures:', len(fails))

title: Signature Contract-driven agent code review
description: Signature edition: Every function the agent writes carries contracts (preconditions, postconditions, invariants). A review agent checks each contract with symbolic execution or testing before merge — the codebase accumulates machine-checked documentation as agents write.
method: Agent emits code + contracts; reviewer runs contract checks (runtime assertion testing + static checks); violations return to the author agent with the failing contract.
usage: Require contracts on all agent-authored functions; make the reviewer a merge gate.

demo.code:
print('contract check:')
print('  pre:  x >= 0')
print('  post: result*result <= x < (result+1)*(result+1)')
print('  500 random tests: all contracts hold -> MERGE')

title: Signature SyGuS syntax-guided synthesis
description: Signature edition: Syntax-Guided Synthesis (SyGuS) constrains the synthesizer to a grammar of allowed constructs plus a semantic spec. The grammar keeps generated code idiomatic and reviewable (no bizarre but 'correct' programs), while the spec guarantees behavior — synthesis with style control.
method: Provide grammar G and spec phi; the solver searches L(G) for a program satisfying phi; standard SyGuS-IF format for tool interop.
usage: Write the grammar to match your codebase idioms; the synthesized code will look like it belongs.

demo.code:
print('SyGuS: grammar allows {+, -, *, if}; spec: f(x) = |x|')
print('synthesized: (if (< x 0) (- 0 x) x)  -- idiomatic, verified')

title: Signature Differential verification against reference
description: Signature edition: When a reference implementation exists, the verifier proves the synthesized version agrees with it on all inputs (bounded or unbounded) instead of proving an abstract spec. Differential verification is often easier than full specification — correctness means 'same as the trusted original'.
method: Encode both programs symbolically; ask the solver for an input where outputs differ; UNSAT means equivalent.
usage: Keep a trusted reference (even a slow one); verify optimized syntheses against it automatically.

demo.code:
print('differential check: ref vs synthesized on 10,000 random inputs')
print('  mismatches: 0 -> EQUIVALENT (bounded proof)')

title: Signature Synthesis repair from failed proofs
description: Signature edition: When verification of human-written code fails, the failed proof pinpoints the broken region; a synthesis agent then searches for a local fix that makes the proof go through. Failed verification becomes a repair work order with the proof obligation as the spec.
method: Run verifier; extract the unprovable subgoal; synthesize a replacement for the implicated code region; re-verify; iterate.
usage: Wire the repair agent to CI: red proofs automatically get repair attempts before human triage.

demo.code:
print('proof failed at: loop invariant too weak')
print('synth proposes stronger invariant: 0 <= i <= n')
print('re-verify: PROVED -> auto-repair merged')

title: Signature Sketch-based program sketching
description: Signature edition: In sketching, the human writes a program with holes (unknown constants, unknown expressions) and the synthesizer fills them to satisfy assertions. It splits the work sensibly: humans provide structure and insight, the machine searches the combinatorial details.
method: Write sketch with ?? holes; encode as SAT/SMT constraints with assertions; solve; substitute the solution back into the sketch.
usage: Sketch the algorithm shape; assert the required behavior; let the solver fill constants and bit-twiddling.

demo.code:
print('sketch: int f(int x) { return x * ??; }')
print('assert f(3) == 21; assert f(4) == 28;')
print('solver fills ?? = 7 -> verified program')

title: Signature Fuzzing as synthesis oracle
description: Signature edition: Fuzzers (AFL++, libFuzzer) bombard synthesized code with mutated inputs hunting for crashes, hangs, and sanitizer violations. A synthesis agent that passes fuzzing has survived adversarial inputs no human would think to try — fuzzing is the verifier for robustness properties.
method: Compile candidate with sanitizers (ASan/UBSan); fuzz with coverage-guided mutation; any crash is a counterexample fed back to synthesis.
usage: Fuzz every synthesized candidate that handles untrusted input; triage crashes into the counterexample set.

demo.code:
print('fuzzing synthesized parser:')
print('  corpus: 1,204 seeds -> coverage-guided mutation')
print('  crash: input b"\\xff\\xfe" -> ASan heap overflow -> counterexample filed')

title: Signature Proof-carrying synthesized code
description: Signature edition: Proof-carrying code attaches a machine-checkable proof to the program: the synthesizer must produce both code and evidence it meets the spec. The consumer checks the proof in milliseconds without trusting the synthesizer — verification is decoupled from (possibly untrusted) synthesis.
method: Synthesizer emits (program, proof); a small trusted checker validates the proof against the spec; only proof-valid programs execute.
usage: Use for untrusted synthesis sources (third-party agents, marketplaces of generated code).

demo.code:
prog, proof = 'sort(xs)', 'proof: permutation + ordered (checked)'
print('program:', prog)
print('checker verdict:', 'VALID' if 'checked' in proof else 'REJECT')
